title_en: Xia Shanrong v. Xuzhou City Construction Bureau — dispute over administrative certification
ruling_gist_en: 1. The competent administrative department of construction's organization of a comprehensive completion inspection and acceptance of a residential community built on collectively-owned land and issuance of an acceptance certificate does not contravene the legislative intent of the Regulations on the Administration of Urban Real Estate Development and Operation, which provides that 'a real estate development project may be delivered for use only after it is completed and accepted as qualified.' This is a specific administrative act performed by the department in accordance with its authority. Such act directly affects the interests of the residents of the residential community and is an actionable specific administrative act.
keywords_en: Administrative; Administrative certification dispute; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Natural person; Legal person; State organ; Regulations on the Administration of Urban Real Estate Development and Operation; Administrative Measures for Comprehensive Completion Inspection and Acceptance of Urban Residential Communities; Justiciability of comprehensive completion inspection and acceptance of residential communities; Public credibility of acceptance certificate and review responsibility; Admission and procurement of new evidence for retrial; Reversal of judgment; Comprehensive completion inspection and acceptance of residential communities; Relocation resettlement housing; Uninstalled electric meter; Principle of public credibility; Guarantee; Warranty; Administrative litigation; Administrative certification dispute with Xuzhou Construction Bureau
full_text_en:
Xia Shanrong v. Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction — dispute over administrative certification

Ruling Summary

1. The administrative department in charge of construction organizing comprehensive completion inspection and issuing a completion inspection certificate for a residential community built on collectively-owned land does not violate the legislative intent of the "Regulations on the Development and Management of Urban Real Estate" that "a real estate development project shall only be delivered for use after being completed and passing inspection." This is a specific administrative act performed by the department in exercising its authority. Such an act directly affects the interests of residents in the residential community and is an actionable specific administrative act.

2. The administrative department in charge of construction is the organizer and final examiner of comprehensive completion inspection for residential communities within its administrative region, exercising the power of comprehensive completion inspection on behalf of the state. The "Residential Completion Inspection Certificate" issued by the administrative department in charge of construction after the comprehensive completion inspection is passed serves to guarantee, with the credibility of a government agency, that the construction quality of the residential community has reached a level suitable for delivery and use. Before issuing the certificate, the administrative department in charge of construction must ensure that every fact certified in the certificate is true, to avoid undermining the credibility of the government agency. If a fact certified in the certificate is false, the administrative department in charge of construction shall bear legal liability for dereliction of duty in review.

3. In an administrative lawsuit tried through the trial supervision procedure, the parties shall provide new evidence discovered after the expiration of the evidence submission period in the original trial in accordance with the law. If a party is genuinely unable to collect such evidence due to objective reasons and has provided relevant leads, the party may apply to the people's court for obtaining the evidence, and the people's court may also, on its own initiative, obtain evidence from administrative agencies, other organizations, or citizens. After cross-examination and authentication of the new evidence, if the main facts on which the specific administrative act under review is based cannot be established, the original specific administrative act shall be annulled by amended judgment.

Plaintiff: Xia Shanrong, female, 55 years old, farmer from Guanzhuang Village, Kuishan Township, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, temporarily residing in the vegetable plot at the west section of Hubei Road, Xuzhou City.

Defendant: Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, Jiangsu Province, domiciled at: Jiefang Road, Xuzhou City.

Legal Representative: Guo Zongming, Director of the Bureau.

Third Party: Xuzhou Hengxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Province, domiciled at: Zhongshan South Road, Xuzhou City.

Legal Representative: Wen Yuan, General Manager of the Company.

On June 18, 2001, the Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, issued to the Third Party, Xuzhou Hengxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengxin Real Estate Company), the (15) "Residential Completion Inspection Certificate" [hereinafter referred to as Certificate No. 15], certifying that the 1-6 and 11 residential buildings of Century Garden built by Hengxin Real Estate Company had passed expert inspection, scored 80.5 points in the inspection evaluation, met the inspection standards, and were ready for occupancy. The Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, believing that this certificate infringed upon her lawful rights and interests, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Yunlong District People's Court of Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province. The Yunlong District People's Court transferred the case to the Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City, which added Hengxin Real Estate Company as a third party and heard the case in open court.

The Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, alleged: Within the Century Garden community, there was a resettlement house provided to the Plaintiff by the Third Party, Hengxin Real Estate Company. Due to the substandard quality of the house and the Third Party's arrears in transitional housing fees, the Plaintiff initiated a civil lawsuit. During the lawsuit, she learned that Century Garden had been certified as a qualified project by the Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction. The Plaintiff argued that at the time of the Defendant's inspection, the Century Garden residential community had not yet installed electricity meters, clearly failing to meet the conditions for completion qualification. However, the Defendant issued a completion inspection certificate to the Third Party, seriously infringing upon the Plaintiff's interests. The Plaintiff requested the court to annul Certificate No. 15 issued by the Defendant.

The Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, submitted the following evidence:

1. A "Demolition Agreement" to prove that Xia Shanrong was a lawful resident of Century Garden and had the right to claim rights regarding the quality of the house;
2. Seven photographs to prove the existence of quality issues in the houses within Century Garden;
3. A notice to prove that electricity meters had not been installed at the time of completion of the Century Garden residential community, and that the Third Party, Hengxin Real Estate Company, did not start verifying the meters and internal wiring until March 25, 2002.

In addition, the Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, also applied to have witness Xu Jiliang testify in court. The content of Xu Jiliang's testimony was that the photographs submitted by Xia Shanrong reflecting the quality issues of the houses were taken by him; the garbage in the Century Garden residential community had not been cleared, landscaping was incomplete, roads were impassable, and electricity meters were not installed until September 2001, so the conditions for delivering the houses were clearly not met. For these reasons, the relocated residents had repeatedly reported the issues to the municipal government.

The Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, argued: In performing its statutory duties and following statutory procedures, the Defendant issued the completion inspection certificate after organizing an expert panel to conduct a comprehensive inspection of the Century Garden residential community and in accordance with the rectification efforts of the construction unit. The Defendant's act of issuing the certificate to the Third Party, Hengxin Real Estate Company, was unrelated to the facts alleged by the Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, such as "substandard house quality and arrears in transitional housing fees." Therefore, the Plaintiff's claim should be dismissed.

The Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, submitted the following evidence:

1. The "Reply on the Proposal for the Renovation Project of Liuchang East Village, Kuishan Township" prepared by the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Commission, the "Land Use Planning Permit" and "Construction Project Planning Permit" prepared by the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau, the "Notice of Approval for Land Expropriation" prepared by the Xuzhou Municipal Land Administration Bureau, the "Preliminary Inspection Certificate for Construction and Installation Project Quality" issued by the Xuzhou Civil Engineering and Construction Quality Supervision Station, the "Fire Protection Inspection Opinion Letter" issued by the Xuzhou Municipal Public Security Fire Brigade, and the "Property Management Trusteeship Contract," among others, to prove that all individual procedures required for the comprehensive inspection were complete and lawful;
2. The "Residential Completion Inspection Application Form," "Xuzhou City Residential Community Completion Inspection Scoring Standards," and Certificate No. 15 to prove that the comprehensive inspection complied with procedures and requirements;
3. The "Regulations on the Development and Management of Urban Real Estate" promulgated by the State Council, the "Measures for the Comprehensive Management of Completion Inspection of Urban Residential Communities" promulgated by the Ministry of Construction, and the "Notice on Amending the Standards for Residential Community Completion Inspection" issued by the Xuzhou City Construction Committee to prove the legal basis for the specific administrative act of conducting the comprehensive inspection.

The Third Party, Hengxin Real Estate Company, stated: The Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, issued the completion inspection certificate to the Third Party in accordance with statutory procedures to perform statutory duties. The act of issuing the certificate was unrelated to the facts alleged by the Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, such as "substandard house quality and arrears in transitional housing fees." Therefore, the Plaintiff's claim should be dismissed.

After cross-examination and authentication, the Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City found the following facts:

The Xuzhou Municipal Planning Commission approved the construction of the Century Garden community residential buildings in Liuchang Village for the resettlement of villagers whose private houses were demolished during the old city reconstruction in Guanzhuang Village, Kuishan Township, Xuzhou City. The project was entrusted to the Third Party, Hengxin Real Estate Company, for development. The Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, was a villager whose private house was demolished. In July 1999, the Guanzhuang Village Committee of Kuishan Township signed a "Demolition Agreement" with her, stipulating that a resettlement house would be provided to Xia Shanrong in the Century Garden residential community, to be delivered within 18 months. On May 8, 2001, Hengxin Real Estate Company reported to the Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, that the residential buildings in the Century Garden community had been completed and applied for a comprehensive completion inspection, simultaneously submitting various inspection materials required for such inspection. After organizing experts to conduct an on-site inspection, the Century Garden residential community scored a total of 80.5 points, with no items failing the inspection. Accordingly, on June 18, 2001, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction issued Certificate No. 15 to Hengxin Real Estate Company.

It was also found that after notification of the delivery of the Century Garden residential community, electricity supply could be ensured, but the electricity meters were not installed until September 2001.

The Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City held: The Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, is the administrative department in charge of construction in Xuzhou City and has the statutory duty to organize and implement comprehensive completion inspections of urban residential communities. The completion inspection certificate is the medium through which the administrative department in charge of construction performs its comprehensive inspection duties and confirms that the residential community meets the inspection standards. Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction has the subject qualification to issue completion inspection certificates.

The Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, presented evidence showing that after receiving the application materials from the Third Party, Hengxin Real Estate Company, it organized a comprehensive inspection team to conduct an on-site inspection on May 8, 2001. Through the inspection team's on-site examination, assessment, and evaluation, the Century Garden residential community was found to be satisfactory in terms of planning and design, architectural design, project quality, public facilities, municipal infrastructure, and property management, with a total score of 80.5 points, meeting the procedural and substantive requirements stipulated in the State Council's "Regulations on the Development and Management of Urban Real Estate," the Ministry of Construction's "Measures for the Comprehensive Management of Completion Inspection of Urban Residential Communities," and the Xuzhou City Construction Committee's "Notice on Amending the Standards for Residential Community Completion Inspection." The Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, acknowledged the validity of these regulations and normative documents. Based on these documents and the comprehensive inspection results, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction issued Certificate No. 15 to Hengxin Real Estate Company, with clear facts, conclusive evidence, correct application of law, and lawful procedures.

The duty of the Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, was to conduct a comprehensive inspection of the Century Garden residential community, not to assess the quality of individual projects within the community. The "Preliminary Inspection Certificate for Construction and Installation Project Quality" issued by the Xuzhou Civil Engineering and Construction Quality Supervision Station proved that the project quality of the Century Garden residential community met the requirements of the "Xuzhou City Residential Community Completion Inspection Scoring Standards." The failure to install electricity meters in a timely manner in the Century Garden residential community was noted by the experts during the comprehensive inspection, and points were deducted accordingly in the scoring. Although the community had certain local defects, the total score remained passing, and these local defects did not affect the overall project quality of the community. Moreover, the law does not stipulate that installing electricity meters is a necessary condition for comprehensive inspection of a residential community. If the Plaintiff, Xia Shanrong, had objections to the quality of individual projects in the community, she could protect her lawful rights and interests through the construction engineering warranty system or complaint system. Xia Shanrong's attempt to negate the comprehensive completion inspection work of Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction for the Century Garden residential community based on quality issues in individual projects was untenable.

In summary, the Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City, in accordance with Article 54, Paragraph (1), of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on November 26, 2002:

Maintain the validity of Certificate No. 15 issued by the Defendant, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, on June 18, 2001.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, Xia Shanrong refused to accept it and appealed to the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, arguing: Buildings 1-6 and 11 of Century Garden did not comply with current national architectural design standards, and there were unauthorized alterations to the drawings and building structures, resulting in an unattractive overall appearance and other problems. These issues fell under the category of non-conforming items in the acceptance standards for architectural and planning design. There were multiple instances of water leakage in kitchens, bathrooms, and walls, lack of floor drains, incomplete water and electricity installations, and insufficient foundation depth, indicating substandard project quality. The supply of electricity and water was incomplete and could not operate normally, indicating substandard public facilities and municipal infrastructure. Construction debris had not been fully removed at the time of inspection, indicating substandard property management. Residential buildings with so many problems clearly did not meet the conditions for inspection. Under these circumstances, the Appellee, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, nevertheless issued Certificate No. 15 to the Third Party, Hengxin Real Estate Company, violating relevant regulations and should be revoked. The first-instance judgment's findings of fact were unclear and its application of law was erroneous, requesting the second-instance court to revise the judgment.

The Appellee, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, replied: In response to the construction unit's application, the Appellee, after verifying the relevant materials provided, organized an expert panel for an on-site comprehensive inspection on May 8, 2001. It then issued the completion inspection certificate for Buildings 1-6 and 11 of Century Garden based on the rectification efforts of the construction unit. The first-instance judgment accurately found the facts regarding the Appellee's issuance of the certificate and correctly applied the law. The second-instance court should dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The Third Party at First Instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, stated: The Third Party strictly constructed according to standards and drawings, and there were no project quality issues in the Century Garden residential community. The Appellee strictly followed statutory procedures in issuing Certificate No. 15 to the Third Party, which was a lawful administrative act. The second-instance court should affirm the first-instance judgment.

The Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found the case facts to be identical to those of the first instance.

The Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court held: As the administrative department in charge of construction in Xuzhou City, the Appellee, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, had the statutory duty in the comprehensive completion inspection it organized to check whether the land use conditions of the community met requirements, whether the community construction complied with the construction project plan, whether it had inspection certificates for individual projects, and whether it had a fire protection inspection certificate. Issuing the "Construction Project Planning Permit," inspection certificates for individual projects, and fire protection inspection certificates were statutory duties of the corresponding functional departments, which fell outside the scope of the construction department's authority. The correctness of the content of these certificates and the appropriateness of the comprehensive inspection team's scoring were also not within the scope of the construction department's review. The Appellant's claim of substandard project quality contradicted the "Preliminary Inspection Certificate for Construction and Installation Project Quality" issued by the Xuzhou Civil Engineering and Construction Quality Supervision Station. If Xia Shanrong believed that the certificate issued by the Xuzhou Civil Engineering and Construction Quality Supervision Station was erroneous or that there were quality issues with other individual projects, she could pursue other avenues to protect her lawful rights and interests, but such issues were not within the scope of review of this case. As for the Appellant's claims regarding insufficient foundation depth for Buildings 1 and 2, uncleared garbage, and untimely installation of electricity meters, appropriate points had been deducted by the comprehensive inspection team in the scoring, and local defects did not affect the overall comprehensive inspection of the community; therefore, these claims were not supported.

In summary, the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, sufficient evidence, lawful trial procedures, and correct application of law. The Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 61, Paragraph (1), of the Administrative Procedure Law, rendered the following judgment on April 14, 2003:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

After the second-instance judgment was announced, Xia Shanrong still refused to accept it and applied for retrial to the Jiangsu High People's Court. The main reasons were: The "Construction Project Planning Permit" was a document that the Appellee at First Instance, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, was required to review during the comprehensive completion inspection. When the Third Party at First Instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, applied for the comprehensive completion inspection of the residential community, it only submitted a copy of the "Construction Project Planning Permit" No. Xushigui Jian 20010108 (hereinafter referred to as Planning Permit No. 108) to Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction. Upon investigation, it was found that the copy of Planning Permit No. 108 was inconsistent with the content of the stub of the same numbered planning permit retained by the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau. The Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau confirmed that Hengxin Real Estate Company had never obtained a construction project planning permit for the construction of Century Garden and that the bureau intended to impose sanctions on Hengxin Real Estate Company. This fully proved that the copy of Planning Permit No. 108 submitted by Hengxin Real Estate Company was forged evidence. Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction issued Certificate No. 15 to Hengxin Real Estate Company based on the forged planning permit, so the main evidence for issuing the certificate was insufficient. The original judgment's assertion that the certificate issuance by Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction was lawful constituted unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law. The Plaintiff requested a retrial to revoke the original first-instance and second-instance administrative judgments and to annul Certificate No. 15 by amended judgment; and to have Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction bear the litigation costs of the original first and second instances.

To prove that the grounds for retrial were valid, the Retrial Applicant, Xia Shanrong, submitted the "Reply to Xu Jiliang's Letter from the People" (hereinafter referred to as the "Reply") issued by the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau on July 29, 2004. The main content of the "Reply" was: After receiving a report from Xu Jiliang, the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau investigated and found that Hengxin Real Estate Company had not obtained a "Construction Project Planning Permit" for the Century Garden it built. The bureau handled the matter in accordance with the law and intended to make an administrative penalty in accordance with statutory procedures after organizing a hearing. Xia Shanrong also applied to the court to obtain the "Administrative Penalty Decision" No. (2004) Xu Gui Xing Fa Zi 90 (hereinafter referred to as Penalty Decision No. 90) issued by the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau imposing an administrative penalty on Hengxin Real Estate Company.

The Appellee at First Instance, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, replied: As the administrative department in charge of construction in Xuzhou City, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction was merely the organizer of comprehensive completion inspections for urban residential communities within its administrative region. Century Garden was built on collectively-owned land, and for residential communities built on such land, the law does not require that a comprehensive completion inspection be conducted by the administrative department in charge of construction. To protect the interests of resettlement households in the old village reconstruction process and to avoid different delivery standards, and upon the request of the majority of resettlement households and the application of the Third Party at First Instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction conducted a comprehensive completion inspection of Century Garden. During the comprehensive completion inspection, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction only conducted a formal review of the "Construction Project Planning Permit" and was not responsible for verifying its authenticity. Therefore, it was unaware that Hengxin Real Estate Company had not obtained the "Construction Project Planning Permit." Moreover, during the comprehensive inspection, the inspection of the implementation of planning and design for Century Garden was carried out by the staff of the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau who were part of the comprehensive inspection team. The staff of the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau never raised any issues regarding the planning permit during the comprehensive inspection. Although the bureau later discovered problems with the planning permit and imposed an administrative penalty on Hengxin Real Estate Company accordingly, it did not notify Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction of the relevant circumstances. Therefore, even though Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction conducted the comprehensive inspection based on the copy submitted by Hengxin Real Estate Company, as long as the copy was recognized by the planning department, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction could conclude that the planning and design for the Century Garden residential community had been implemented. If the copy was proven to be false, the responsibility could only be borne by the Xuzhou Municipal Planning Bureau, which had recognized the copy. Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, issuing Certificate No. 15 based on the comprehensive completion inspection report submitted by the inspection team, was not improper.

The Appellee at First Instance, Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Construction, submitted the "Meeting Minutes of the General Office of the Municipal Government on the Resettlement Issue of Some Residents in Xiaozhuang" No. 20 (hereinafter referred to as the "Meeting Minutes"), issued by the General Office of Xuzhou Municipal People's Government on May 21, 1999, to prove that the land used for building resettlement houses for farmers in the old village reconstruction in Guanzhuang Village, Kuishan Township, was collectively-owned land. The Retrial Applicant, Xia Shanrong, argued that the "Meeting Minutes" did not bear an official seal and was not new evidence, and could not be used as a basis for establishing facts.

The third party at first instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, alleged: The original of Permit No. 108 was lost due to theft, and therefore Hengxin Real Estate Company submitted a copy of that permit to the appellee at first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau, during the comprehensive completion acceptance of Shiji Huayuan. During the first and second instances, the applicant for retrial, Xia Shanrong, never raised any objection to the authenticity of Construction Permit No. 108. The validity of Construction Permit No. 108 was confirmed through legal procedures. Xuzhou City Construction Bureau's issuance of Acceptance Certificate No. 15 based on the legally effective Construction Permit No. 108 was lawful. If the copy of Construction Permit No. 108 is inconsistent with the contents of the stub of that permit retained by Xuzhou City Planning Bureau, it only proves that the internal management of Xuzhou City Planning Bureau was extremely chaotic. The Penalty Decision No. 90 issued by Xuzhou City Planning Bureau to Hengxin Real Estate Company only concerned the illegal over-construction of some buildings in the Shiji Huayuan project, and did not specify the scope of the over-construction; it is unrelated to the act of issuing the certificate at issue in this case. Xia Shanrong's house was built on collective land. For houses built on collective land, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau had no statutory duty to organize comprehensive completion acceptance. Xuzhou City Construction Bureau organized the comprehensive completion acceptance of Shiji Huayuan only to protect the interests of households relocated due to demolition and resettlement. This was not a specific administrative act performed in the exercise of statutory functions and powers, and therefore does not fall within the scope of administrative litigation accepted by the People's Court.

The third party at first instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, submitted the "Police Dispatch and Handling Registration Form" filled out by the Xuzhou City Public Security Bureau, Pengcheng Police Station, on July 14, 2003, to prove that the original of Construction Permit No. 108 was lost due to theft.

The Jiangsu High People's Court found upon review: Article 52(3) of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Evidence in Administrative Litigation" (hereinafter "Evidence Provisions for Administrative Litigation") provides that evidence discovered by a party after the expiration of the举证期限 is new evidence. When applying for retrial, the applicant for retrial, Xia Shanrong, used the "Reply" as evidence. The "Reply" was made after the original judgment took effect, and Xia Shanrong could not have discovered it within the prescribed period for producing evidence; therefore, it constitutes new evidence. Xia Shanrong's application for retrial with new evidence meets the conditions for retrial, and this case should be placed on file for retrial.

During the retrial, in accordance with Articles 22 and 23(3) of the "Evidence Provisions for Administrative Litigation", upon the application of the applicant for retrial, Xia Shanrong, the Jiangsu High People's Court obtained from Xuzhou City Planning Bureau evidence including the stub of Penalty Decision No. 90 and Construction Permit No. 108, the construction project planning定点批办单, the stub of the approval定点通知书, and the distribution registration records. Penalty Decision No. 90 stated: Hengxin Real Estate Company built 12 buildings in Shiji Huayuan, totaling 49,139.9 m², of which 5,049.4 m² exceeded the planning fixed point, violating Article 19 of the "Measures of Xuzhou City for the Administration of Urban Planning". Pursuant to Articles 37 and 38 of these Measures, it was decided to fine Hengxin Real Estate Company RMB 49,527. After paying the fine, it should go through the planning approval procedures in accordance with regulations. The stub of Construction Permit No. 108, the construction project planning定点批办单, the stub of the approval定点通知书, and the distribution registration records proved that the construction unit of Construction Permit No. 108 was Xuzhou City Kuishan Agricultural Housing Comprehensive Development Company, the project name was Commercial and Residential Buildings (1-8#), the construction location was on the south side of Taishan Road, and the construction scale was 40,930 square meters. However, the copy of Construction Permit No. 108 submitted to the appellee at first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau, by the third party at first instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, indicated the construction unit as Hengxin Real Estate Company, the project name as Residential Buildings (1-11#), the construction location as Liuchang East Village, north side of Hubei Road, and the construction scale as 66,800 square meters. Although the numbers of the two construction permits were the same, their contents were completely different.

During the retrial court hearing, after cross-examination and debate, the parties had the following two disputes regarding the facts of the case:

1. Was the land on which the Shiji Huayuan residential community was located collectively owned or state-owned? The applicant for retrial, Xia Shanrong, argued that the nature of the land on which the Shiji Huayuan residential community was located had changed from collective land to state-owned land; therefore, the appellee at first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau, had the responsibility to organize comprehensive completion acceptance for the Shiji Huayuan residential community. Xuzhou City Construction Bureau argued that the land on which the Shiji Huayuan residential community was located was still collective land. To protect the interests of households relocated during the old village reconstruction process, and upon the request of the majority of relocated households and the application of the third party at first instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, it organized the comprehensive completion acceptance for Shiji Huayuan. Carrying out this work did not constitute performing its statutory duties. Hengxin Real Estate Company argued that the land on which the Shiji Huayuan residential community was located was collective land, and organizing comprehensive completion acceptance for a residential community built on collective land was not a statutory duty of Xuzhou City Construction Bureau. Disputes arising from this also did not fall within the scope of administrative litigation accepted by the People's Court. The court held that during the first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau submitted the Reply to the Proposal for the Renovation Project of Liuchang East Village, Kuishan Township, Xu Ji Tou (1996) No. 184 from Xuzhou City Planning Commission, and the Construction Land Planning Permit, Xu Shi Gui Di (99) No. 95 from Xuzhou City Planning Bureau. This evidence was sufficient to prove that the land where the Shiji Huayuan residential community was located was collective land. The parties had no dispute over this during the first and second instances. During the retrial, although Xia Shanrong claimed that the land on which the Shiji Huayuan residential community was located had changed from collective to state-owned, he did not provide new evidence to support this claim; therefore, this claim could not be established.

2. Was the copy of Construction Permit No. 108 authentic? The applicant for retrial, Xia Shanrong, using the "Reply" as evidence, alleged that the third party at first instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, had forged Construction Permit No. 108. Hengxin Real Estate Company, using the "Police Dispatch and Handling Registration Form" as evidence, argued that the original of Construction Permit No. 108 was lost, and therefore a copy was submitted to the appellee at first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau. To explain the inconsistency between the copy and the contents of the stub of Construction Permit No. 108, Hengxin Real Estate Company stated that "the management of Xuzhou City Planning Bureau was extremely chaotic." The court held that the "Police Dispatch and Handling Registration Form" only recorded the content of the alarm and the losses, but did not record the names of the stolen documents, and thus could not prove that Hengxin Real Estate Company had ever held the original of Construction Permit No. 108. The stub of Construction Permit No. 108 retained by Xuzhou City Planning Bureau, whose contents were corroborated by other evidence such as the simultaneously archived construction project planning定点批办单, stub of the approval定点通知书, and distribution registration records, was authentic. However, the copy of Construction Permit No. 108 submitted by Hengxin Real Estate Company had contents that not only were inconsistent with the stub of Construction Permit No. 108 but also were not supported by any other evidence. Accordingly, it was determined that the copy of Construction Permit No. 108 submitted by Hengxin Real Estate Company was false and forged evidence.

Apart from the two points above, the parties had no objection to other facts determined in the original instance, which were confirmed in the retrial.

The issues in dispute to be resolved in the retrial were: 1. Regarding the Shiji Huayuan residential community built on collective land, was Xuzhou City Construction Bureau's issuance of an acceptance certificate after organizing the comprehensive completion acceptance an actionable administrative act? 2. After the copy of Construction Permit No. 108 was found to be forged evidence, who should bear the responsibility?

The Jiangsu High People's Court held after trial:

I. Article 17 of the State Council's "Regulations on the Administration of Urban Real Estate Development and Operation" provides: "Real estate development projects shall not be delivered for use until they have been completed and passed acceptance inspection; those that have not been inspected or have failed inspection shall not be delivered for use." "After the completion of a real estate development project, the real estate development enterprise shall submit a completion acceptance application to the competent department for real estate development of the local people's government at or above the county level where the project is located. The competent department for real estate development shall, within 30 days from the date of receiving the completion acceptance application, organize relevant departments or units such as engineering quality supervision, planning, fire protection, and civil air defense to conduct an acceptance inspection on matters involving public safety." Article 3, paragraph 3 of the Ministry of Construction's "Administrative Measures for the Comprehensive Completion Acceptance of Urban Residential Communities" provides: "The construction administrative department of the city people's government shall be responsible for organizing and implementing the comprehensive completion acceptance of urban residential communities within its administrative region." Although current laws, regulations, and rules provide that the construction administrative department is responsible for organizing the comprehensive completion acceptance of urban residential communities within its administrative region, the construction administrative department's organization of comprehensive completion acceptance for residential communities built on collective land does not contravene the legislative intent of "real estate development projects shall not be delivered for use until they have been completed and passed acceptance inspection." Regardless of whether the land on which the Shiji Huayuan residential community was located was state-owned or collectively owned, the appellee at first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau, must exercise its administrative functions and powers to organize the comprehensive completion acceptance for this residential community. Issuing Acceptance Certificate No. 15 after the comprehensive completion acceptance directly affected the interests of residents of the Shiji Huayuan residential community and constituted an actionable administrative act. The argument of the third party at first instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, that Xuzhou City Construction Bureau's act of issuing Acceptance Certificate No. 15 for Shiji Huayuan did not fall within the scope of administrative litigation was unfounded.

II. Article 18, paragraph 1 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Urban Real Estate Development and Operation" provides: "For the completion of group real estate development projects such as residential communities, comprehensive acceptance shall be carried out in accordance with Article 17 of these Regulations and the following requirements: (1) the implementation of urban planning design conditions; (2) the construction of supporting infrastructure and public facilities required by urban planning; (3) the completion acceptance of individual engineering works; (4) the implementation of demolition and resettlement plans; (5) the implementation of property management." Article 8, paragraph 1 of the "Administrative Measures for the Comprehensive Completion Acceptance of Urban Residential Communities" provides: "The comprehensive completion acceptance of a residential community shall be carried out in accordance with the following procedures: (1) After all construction projects of the residential community are completed, the development and construction unit shall submit to the construction administrative department of the city people's government a comprehensive completion acceptance application report, together with the documents and materials specified in Article 6 of these Measures; (2) Within one month after receiving the comprehensive completion acceptance application report and relevant materials, the construction administrative department of the city people's government shall form a comprehensive acceptance team composed of relevant departments including urban construction (including municipal engineering, public utilities, landscaping, environmental sanitation), planning, real estate, engineering quality supervision, and the residential community operation management unit; (3) The comprehensive acceptance team shall review the relevant acceptance materials, hear the report from the development and construction unit, conduct on-site inspections, comprehensively appraise and evaluate the construction and management of the residential community, formulate acceptance opinions, and submit the comprehensive completion acceptance report for the residential community to the construction administrative department of the city people's government; (4) The construction administrative department of the city people's government shall review the comprehensive acceptance report. After the comprehensive acceptance report is reviewed and deemed qualified, the development and construction unit may proceed with the delivery procedures for the houses and related facilities."

Pursuant to the above provisions, as the construction administrative department of the Xuzhou City People's Government, the appellee at first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau, was lawfully exercising the power of comprehensive completion acceptance on behalf of the state for the Shiji Huayuan residential community. After the comprehensive completion acceptance was deemed qualified, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau's issuance of the "Residential Housing Completion Acceptance Certificate" to the third party at first instance, Hengxin Real Estate Company, relied on the credibility of the government organs formed by state public power to guarantee that the construction quality of the residential community had reached the level suitable for delivery and use. Before issuing this certificate, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau had to ensure that every fact on which the certificate was based was true, so as not to undermine the credibility of the government organs. During the comprehensive completion acceptance, although Xuzhou City Construction Bureau did not directly review all acceptance materials, it organized the comprehensive acceptance team and had the duty to review the comprehensive completion acceptance report for the residential community submitted by the comprehensive acceptance team. The "Construction Project Planning Permit" was one of the acceptance materials attached to the comprehensive completion acceptance report for the residential community. The authenticity of this permit was, of course, subject to prior review by the staff of Xuzhou City Planning Bureau who participated in the comprehensive acceptance team. However, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau could not thereby shirk its own responsibility for final review. Especially where Hengxin Real Estate Company only submitted a copy of Construction Permit No. 108, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau should have exercised even more careful review. Xuzhou City Construction Bureau failed to detect that the copy of Construction Permit No. 108 was forged evidence, and issued Acceptance Certificate No. 15 based on this forged evidence; it shall bear the legal responsibility for dereliction of duty in review. Acceptance Certificate No. 15 was the conclusion drawn by Xuzhou City Construction Bureau after the comprehensive completion acceptance of the Shiji Huayuan residential community. This conclusion was based on false evidence and therefore cannot serve to prove that the Shiji Huayuan residential community had passed acceptance inspection and was suitable for delivery and use. Xuzhou City Construction Bureau's issuance of Acceptance Certificate No. 15 to Hengxin Real Estate Company lacked main evidence and improperly applied laws and regulations; it should be revoked.

Given that in the original first and second instances, the applicant for retrial, Xia Shanrong, did not file the lawsuit on the ground that the planning and design conditions for Shiji Huayuan had not been implemented, and none of the parties raised any objection to the authenticity of Construction Permit No. 108 during the proceedings, the courts of first and second instance determined the facts based on the evidence known at the time and rendered judgments maintaining the specific administrative act in question. This did not violate legal provisions. During the retrial, it was found that the evidence on which the original first and second instance judgments were based had changed, and the factual basis for the original first and second instance judgments no longer existed. Therefore, the retrial should change the judgment according to law. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 54, paragraph (2), items 1 and 2, and Article 61, paragraph (2) of the Administrative Procedure Law, and Articles 76, paragraph 1 and 78 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretations on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China", the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered judgment on March 6, 2006:

1. The administrative judgment of the second instance is reversed; the administrative judgment of the first instance is reversed;
2. Acceptance Certificate No. 15 issued by the appellee at first instance, Xuzhou City Construction Bureau, on June 18, 2001, is revoked.

This judgment is final.

After the judgment was changed in the retrial, to properly resolve the administrative dispute and promote administration according to law, the Jiangsu High People's Court, by way of a judicial suggestion on March 13, 2006, notified the Xuzhou City People's Government of the circumstances of this case, pointing out: Certain administrative organs and their staff forging official documents of the state has seriously affected the normal order of national administrative management, damaged the integrity of the government, and can easily trigger administrative disputes and intensify conflicts between officials and citizens, which is detrimental to building a rule-of-law Jiangsu and a harmonious society. It was suggested that the Xuzhou City People's Government investigate the responsibility of the relevant personnel for forging official documents according to law.
